versions.analysis_for_next:
Neutral recall is the main weakness: 33 neutral texts were called positive and 24 negative, while 14 positive and 14 negative texts were called neutral. Patterns:
(1) Neutral called positive. These are plain plans or logistics ('going to the game Friday', 'bowling tomorrow', 'see the movie tomorrow'), fan requests or wishes ('we want you to come', 'please sing at my wedding'), questions, trivia, jokes and spam. The model takes '!!!', 'lol' or a fun topic as enough for positive. Fix: positive needs an explicit positive feeling or evaluation; an upbeat activity or topic alone is neutral.
(2) Neutral called negative. These are light self-deprecating or joking gripes ('lmao', 'I'm dead', procrastinating, 'not ready', 'Nooo... #peak') and wry or sarcastic commentary on sports or politics. Fix: playful or joking gripes and wry remarks are neutral unless there is real distress, anger or criticism. V0 told the model that self-deprecation is negative, so remove that.
(3) Negative called neutral. These are news about harmful events (deficit, missile strike, charged with IRA membership, funeral, a phone breaking) and argumentative replies. Fix: a report of an inherently bad event (violence, death, loss, crime, damage) is negative even when written as a headline.
(4) Positive called neutral. These are wins or titles in sports, promotions inviting people (tickets, giveaways, info sessions), and historic or hopeful news. Fix: report a victory, achievement, milestone or invitation as positive.
I will keep the cue lists shorter and the whole question under 300 words.

Version 1 raised neutral recall and macro-F1 went from 68.8 to 72.6. However, positive recall fell: 24 positive texts were called neutral.
(1) Positive called neutral. These are mostly personal plans or anticipation of something enjoyable ('going to watch X tomorrow', 'standing at Wrigley for Foo Fighters tomorrow', 'fast forward to the concert', 'celebrate all day', 'Bee Gees on loop', 'perfect friday night'). Annotators treat an author looking forward to or doing something they like as positive, even without explicit emotion words. V1 told the model plans are neutral, which overcorrected.
(2) Neutral called positive. These are organization-style announcements and registrations (free info morning, sign up for a walk, trunk show, ministry meeting), detached sports results or game updates, and mildly favorable news or opinion. Fix: impersonal event listings, promos and registrations are neutral, and so are game results reported without cheering.
(3) Negative called neutral. These are implied criticism or complaint: rhetorical or accusing questions ('why did they bomb', 'don't know why they haven't...'), sarcastic jabs ('Desperation Day', 'no talent'), grudging remarks ('not cause I enjoy it'). Fix: say that implied disapproval, sarcasm aimed at someone and grumbling count as negative.
(4) Neutral called negative. These are hyperbolic fan or self-joking gripes and mildly bad sports or news facts. Keep the playful-gripe rule as neutral.
The plan is to restore personal anticipation and enjoyment as positive, move impersonal promos and results to neutral, and add implied criticism to negative.

Version 2 dropped macro-F1 from 72.6 to 70.5. Calling personal plans positive pushed many neutral texts into positive (30). Examples are 'going to the Blue Jays game', 'going to Chase Bryant', 'thinking of road tripping', 'wonder whether to see a movie'. Annotators label bare plans neutral, and label plans positive only when enthusiasm is expressed ('can't wait', 'fast forward to', 'celebrate all day', vivid anticipation). The implied-criticism rule caught a few negatives but added neutral-to-negative errors, such as dry jokes about athletes and sarcasm at a company.
Positives still missed:
- Reports of wins or titles (Serena, Federer, McGregor), where the model treats the reporting as detached.
- Promos with an enticement (win a car, free scoop, who wants tickets, get your tickets now, film masterpiece opens).
- Positive news (delighted, history was made, hilariously stole the show).
Annotators clearly label win reports and enticing promos positive, while plain listings without an enticement and sign-up logistics lean neutral.
Plan: return to the v1 structure. Plans are neutral unless they carry enthusiasm. Win or title reports and upbeat news are positive even when stated factually. Promos offering prizes, free items, tickets or praise are positive. Keep negative close to v1, adding only clear sarcastic mockery of a person.

Version 3 is the best so far: macro-F1 74.6. The remaining errors are spread thinly and many look like label noise, so I will make only small, targeted changes.
(1) Positive called neutral (19). Several are the author inviting others to join their own outing or event ('come support the team', 'come with us!!', 'please share', 'let's go!'). Others show the author happily indulging in something they like ('Bee Gees on loop, don't hate', 'for sure going to watch X', 'reread for the 7th time'). Fix: an author's invitation to join their event, or committed, eager participation in a favorite activity, counts as positive. Bare plans stay neutral.
(2) Neutral called positive (21). These are mid-game sports updates and close-call commentary, mild political comparisons, speculative good-news headlines ('may not come to pass', 'may be positioning'), celebrity births and birthdays reported in wire style, and spam offering free items. Fix: in-progress game updates, speculative or comparative opinions, and wire-style celebrity life events are neutral; spam is neutral even when it says 'free'. Only completed wins or titles count as positive.
(3) Negative called neutral (16). These are implied complaints and mild digs ('I don't know why they haven't...', 'Desperation Day', 'no talent', 'so confused'). Fix: note that a short grumble or dig at something counts as negative even without strong words. Keep jokey self-mockery neutral to avoid shifting the neutral-to-negative errors.
The rest of v3 stays as it is.

Version 4 is the best so far: macro-F1 77.3. Most remaining errors are borderline or noisy, so I will make only careful refinements.
(1) Neutral called negative (20) is now the largest error cell. Many are joking jabs at public figures, teams or companies delivered with a comic tone ('Bwahaha', 'didn't get the memo', 'clear as mud', 'padding up his numbers', 'Could be worse'). Others are minor personal hiccups reported matter-of-factly with a workaround or apology ('computer broke, may try Xbox', 'wrong track was played'). Others are fandom melodrama ('v sad', 'not ready', 'Nooo... #peak'). Fix: describe these explicitly as neutral, separate from earnest complaints.
(2) Neutral called positive (16). These are group meetups and hangout promos (ministry meeting, trunk show with complimentary items) and in-progress game excitement. Fix: routine group meetings and listings are neutral even when friendly. Keep promos that push tickets or prizes as positive.
(3) Negative called neutral (15). These are implicit complaints, argumentative questions and digs. I will keep the v4 negative description and add argumentative rhetorical questions.
Otherwise keep v4 intact.

The version 6 draft ran over the limit at 307 words, so I trimmed wording while keeping the same changes. Version 5 is the best so far, with macro-F1 79.9, and its remaining errors are mostly borderline or noisy. The tweaks stay small and low-risk:
- Positive: add festive greetings, holidays, birthday wishes and eager anticipation of releases.
- Neutral: add casual status updates ('now watching', 'sounds like the move') and speculative opinions ('may', 'I think').
- Negative: unchanged, because that boundary is balanced.
To save words I shortened the instructions and compressed the cue lists.

Version 6 scored 80.3, a slight gain, but positive-to-neutral errors rose from 15 to 17. Two causes are visible:
- When compressing I dropped the cue 'perfect night', and 'Popcorn and Seinfeld sounds like the perfect friday night' became neutral.
- The new neutral rule for speculative opinions ('I think', 'I believe') pulled a hopeful prediction about a favorite player winning a title to neutral, along with a remark about a fast win.
Fixes: restore 'perfect' as a positive cue, and say that rooting for or predicting success of a favored person counts as positive. Narrow the speculative-neutral rule to detached or mixed speculation. Remove 'sounds like the move' as a neutral example because it conflicts with the 'perfect' phrasing.
The other cells are stable, so I will trim words elsewhere to stay under 300.

Version 7 fell to 79.3 from v6's 80.3, so I am going back to v6 nearly unchanged.
- The 'rooting for or predicting success' rule pushed mild political and TV opinions (Kasich, Briana) to positive.
- Dropping 'sounds like the move' from neutral sent a casual status remark ('Jacksonville sounds like the move') to positive.
- Compressing 'a champion wins or reaches a final' to 'a champion wins' lost the Federer final.
The one v7 change worth keeping is 'perfect night' as a positive cue. To keep the length under 300 words, I removed 'conflict' from the negative list.

Version 8 (80.0) is essentially tied with v6 (80.3). Restoring 'perfect night' fixed the 'perfect friday night' text, but removing 'conflict' from negative may have cost the 'charged with IRA membership granted bail' headline, which dropped to neutral at 0.52. The remaining errors are mostly label noise or contradictory cases. Examples are a lesser seed's win labelled neutral while champions' wins are labelled positive, and comic jabs labelled neutral while similar digs are labelled negative.
Plan: keep the v6 and v8 structure. Restore crimes, conflict and violence in negative, and make 'charged or bailed' explicit. To stay under 300 words, cut the promo cue list to one example.

Version 9 matches v6's best score: macro-F1 80.3, with 64 errors. Each label now has 15–31 errors, and most of them are contradictory or noisy cases:
- Lesser-seed wins are labelled neutral while champion wins are labelled positive.
- Comic jabs are labelled neutral while similar digs are labelled negative.
- Ticket promos are labelled positive while meetups are labelled neutral.
Attempts to recover hopeful predictions (v7) and other tweaks cost more than they gained. For the final version I keep v9's tested wording essentially unchanged, because further edits risk lowering the score without a reliable gain.
